key_errors: FAILED tests/llm/accuracy_conformance.py::test_accuracy_conformance[Qwen/Qwen2-0.5B-Instruct-INT8-GPU] - AssertionError: Metric drop 0.05254477262496948 exceeds threshold 0.03
root_cause: The failed job (LLM accuracy iGPU tests) is unrelated to this PR's diff, which only touches GPU plugin dual-runtime dispatch/build infrastructure (core_impl, plugin registration, CMake) and does not change the LLM accuracy pipeline, Qwen2 model handling, or GPU inference numerics for the default single-runtime OCL path exercised by this job. This exact failure signature (Qwen2-0.5B-Instruct-INT8-GPU metric drop of ~0.0525 vs 0.03 threshold) has now recurred 4 times across unrelated PRs since 2026-08-27, indicating a known intermittent accuracy flake in the LLM accuracy GPU test (likely driven by run-to-run numerical variance near the threshold boundary) rather than a regression introduced by any single PR.
reproduction_steps: Run `pytest tests/llm/accuracy_conformance.py::test_accuracy_conformance -k Qwen2-0.5B-Instruct-INT8-GPU` on a GPU-enabled runner multiple times; the metric drop value fluctuates near the 0.03 threshold and occasionally exceeds it.
recommended_actions: Re-run only the failed job (already recorded in the pattern database with 4 occurrences) — no PR code change is needed for this specific failure.

Investigate whether the 0.03 threshold for Qwen2-0.5B-Instruct-INT8-GPU is too tight given observed run-to-run variance (~0.05 metric drop seen repeatedly), and consider widening it or adding averaging/seed pinning if not already done.
Track CVS ticket for this specific model/threshold combination if one does not already exist, referencing the recurring pattern hash 47caedf70a4041f8.
prevention_strategies: Add variance/seed stabilization to the Qwen2-0.5B-Instruct-INT8-GPU accuracy check, or increase its threshold margin with justified statistical analysis, to reduce false-positive merge-queue failures for unrelated PRs.
historical_context: Same signature previously recorded on 2026-08-27 (PR #37611), 2026-08-27 (PR #37768, later investigation), and 2026-09-03 (PR #37799) — all with the same or very similar assertion message. This is the 4th occurrence in the CI Doctor MQ pattern database.
